comments.text:
There are multiple issues.  Two that I see that are usually not mentioned.  One is that colleges graduate twice as many people per year than there are jobs that require a degree.  Remove the STEM degrees and it gets much worse.  Anything in oversupply goes down in value.  All about 50% of the graduates got was a piece of paper and long term debt.  My wife works a job with tech training.  They get multiple applicants with college degrees since they cannot find jobs in their field.  Due to attitude of the applicants that is I have a degree you do not, they are very picky about hiring anyone with a degree.  A degree is truly not needed for her job, but a strong work ethic, thinking on your feet, organization, and being somewhat OCD are.  The ones with degrees usually fail those requirements.

Two,  I saw this as I hired.  I hold a masters in engineering.  A degree used to mean that the basic ability to problem solve, analyze situation, communicate with people were present.  In my last 10 years of hiring I have found those skills increasingly weaker.  In fact I have found some applicants that had issues with basic reading, communication, and math.  Lots of bravado but no skills.   I got grief from HR for taking the person without a degree at times.  I needed a job done.  I hired the person most likely to be able to do the job.  By year one of their hire, I had been proven to be right in my choices.

comments.text: Listen, Degrees may be USELESS for a big-paying job, but at least they can get you an easy job. I got a degree in 2010, am I making bank? Are they entry level jobs? Some of them, but at least I get the interviews and the position. It is all about what you have done (results at previous jobs) and how you present yourself (and to charm them, YOU NEED TO GET THE INTERVIEW. My bachelor's is in Hospitality and Tourism, my experience is in hotel operations and corporate / private events. Was my degree fancy? NO! But because my degree was NOT FANCY and because of my grades and other scholarships I applied for, I graduated with 20k in debt (living on campus), I was able to pay off my debt (paying $$550 eaxh month and living with a roommate, and I survived.  Hospitality is a PAIN as an industry but you will ALWAYS find they are hiring and if you look at the bright side, you can get to enjoy the experience.
